nodes.name: Hydrothermal synthesis
nodes.procedure: Precursors, including ammonium tungstate as metal source and pre-treated Ni foam (denoted as NF) as three-dimension substrate, were treated by the hydrothermal method (180°C;6h) to obtain defect-free hexagonal tungsten trioxide.
nodes.source_text: precursors, including ammonium tungstate as metal source and pre-treated Ni foam (denoted as NF) as three-dimension substrate (Figure S1, Supporting Information), were treated by the hydrothermal method (180°C;6h) to obtain defect-free hexagonal tungsten trioxide.

nodes.name: Joule heating phase transformation
nodes.procedure: The rapid Joule heating reaction at 923.15K was conducted to induce the phase transformation for tungsten oxide from hexagonal WO3 to monoclinic WOx with metallic properties due to unique W-W bonding. The reductive atmosphere (10% H2/Ar) during the rapid self-heating/cooling process (60 s) endows oxides with local unsaturation of metal sites to achieve rich defects.

nodes.name: UV photoreduction
nodes.procedure: The in situ Ru nanoparticles immobilization on WOx was realized via direct UV light reduction in RuCl3 solution (denoted as RWO)(details in Experimental Section).

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM shows Ru nanoparticles (≈4.5 nm) decorated on WOx with lattice spacings of 0.234 nm and 0.183 nm matching (100) Ru and (-301) WO2 planes; RWO has hollow nanoneedle structure with average pore diameter 7.79 nm.
nodes.evidence_snippet: (Transmission electron microscope) TEM image in Figure 1e indicated successful decoration of Ru nanoparticles (≈4.5 nm) on WOx, with measured lattice spacings of 0.234 nm and 0.183 nm, which were well matched with the (100) and (-301) planes of Ru and WO2...

nodes.characterization_summary: EDX mapping shows uniform distribution of Ru, W, O elements in RWO with ratio 1.39%:31.27%:67.34%.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 1g showed energy dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDX) mapping results, clearly revealing the uniform distribution of Ru, W and O elements across the RWO with ratio of 1.39%:31.27%:67.34% (Table S1, Supporting Information).

nodes.characterization_summary: RWO W 4f shows mixed W4+ (4f7/2=33.89 eV, 4f5/2=35.96 eV; 59.69%) and W6+ (4f7/2=35.58 eV, 4f5/2=37.65 eV; 40.31%) with 0.38 eV positive shift vs WOx; Ru 3d shows Ru0 (3d5/2=280.93 eV; 76.6%), Ru3+ (281.90 eV), Ru4+ (282.47 eV); O 1s shows Ov at 531.66 eV (28.55%).
nodes.evidence_snippet: As illustrated in W 4f spectra... characterized by mixed W4+ (4f7/2 = 33.89 eV, 4f5/2 = 35.96 eV) and W6+ (4f7/2 = 35.58 eV, 4f5/2 = 37.65 eV) species in WOx. The high W4+/W6+ ratio of 59.69:40.31... the Ru 3d spectrum... could be deconvolved into three characteristic peaks including metallic Ru0 (3d5/2 = 280.93 eV), Ru3+ (3d5/2 = 281.90 eV) and Ru4+ (3d5/2 = 282.47 eV).

nodes.characterization_summary: RWO-A shows characteristic peaks of WO2 at (011), (101), (200), and (220) planes, consistent with RWO.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Besides, the XRD pattern of the RWO-A also showed characteristic peaks of WO2 at (011), (101), (200), and (220) planes, consistent with the SEM and XRD results of RWO (Figure 3f).

nodes.characterization_summary: High-resolution SEM confirms 3D hierarchical nanoneedle architecture retained in RWO-A.
nodes.evidence_snippet: And the high-resolution SEM (Figure 3g) confirmed the 3D hierarchical nanoneedle architecture on NF, demonstrating the retained main phase structure of RWO during the electrochemical activation process.

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM shows Ru-based particles size distribution in RWO-A at 1.60 nm, similar to RWO (1.58 nm).
nodes.evidence_snippet: Besides, the size distribution of Ru-based particles in RWO-A was also investigated, which was in the range of 1.60 nm as shown in Figure 3h.

nodes.characterization_summary: RWO-A Ru 3d XPS shows Run+ (0<n≤4) content increased from 23.4% (initial RWO) to 89.4% after 40 CV cycles confirming in situ oxidation; W 4f peaks at W4+ (34.45/36.52 eV) and W6+ (35.62/37.81 eV) similar to RWO.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Quantitative XPS analysis (Figure 3d) confirmed obvious oxidation of metallic Ru0 (3d5/2 = 280.89 eV) to Ru3+ (3d5/2 = 282.46 eV) and Ru4+ (3d5/2 = 281.90 eV), wherein the increased content of Run+ (0<n≤4) from 23.4% to 89.4%... The W 4f XPS spectra of RWO-A (Figure S13, Supporting Information) displayed two characteristic peaks at W 4f7/2 (35.62 eV for W6+ and 34.45 eV for W4+)...

nodes.characterization_summary: In situ Raman of RWO shows WO2 peaks at 168, 190, 290, 620, 788 cm-1; RuOx peak emerges at 521 cm-1 and W-OH at ~1167 cm-1 during cathodic potential, confirming dynamic reconstruction and proton insertion.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Figure 4a, initial spectra of pristine RWO exhibited characteristic WO2 peaks at 168, 190, 290, 620 and 788 cm-1... By shifting the potential positively from +0.025 V to -0.1 V, the vibrational frequencies for the peak located at 521 cm-1 emerged...
